source_text: τριβόμενοι μολυσμὸν, καὶ διὰ τούτων ἂν γένοιτο παντί τῳ σαφές. Λέγωμεν δὲ ἀνὰ μέρος τὰ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν γεγραμμένων· προήκοι γὰρ ἂν εὐκρινῶς ὁ λόγος καὶ διαπτύσσων, ὡς ἔνι, τὰ κεκρυμμένα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Λαμβάνεται τοίνυν ὁ μόσχος ἀμώμητός τε καὶ ἀπλὴξ εἰς τύπον Χριστοῦ τοῦ ἀληθῶς ἀμώμου, καὶ τὸν ἐκ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τραυματισμὸν οὐκ ἀνασχομένου παθεῖν. «Ἔρχεται γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, καὶ ἐν ἐμοὶ εὑρήσει οὐδέν·» οὐ γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Προσάγεται δὲ πρὸς αὐταῖς τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς ταῖς θύραις ἔναντι Κυρίου, τὸ παθεῖν ὥσπερ οὐ παραιτούμενος, ὑπέρ γε τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, ἀνατεθειμένος τε ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἔφασκεν, «Ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐγὼ ἁγιάζω ἐμαυτόν.» Τὸ, ἁγιάζω, λέγων, ἀντὶ τοῦ, προσάγω, καὶ ἀνατίθημι προσφορὰν ἀμώμητον τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί. Ἁγιάζεσθαι γὰρ λέγεται τὸ ἀνατιθέμενον τῷ Θεῷ, κατ' ἐκεῖνό που τὸ γεγραμμένον· «Παγὶς ἀνδρὶ, ταχύ τι τῶν ἰδίων ἁγιάσαι· μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εὔξασθαι, μετανοεῖν γίνεται.» Ὅτι δὲ ἡ προσφορὰ δεκτὴ καὶ εὐάρεστος, δηλοῖ τὸ, «Ἔναντι Κυρίου.» Νοοῦμεν γὰρ ἤδη τὸ γεγραμμένον ἐπὶ τῆς τῶν ἀδελφῶν ξυνωρίδος, Καΐν τέ φημι καὶ Ἀβέλ. «Ἐπεῖδε μὲν γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ Ἀβέλ τε καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ, ἐπὶ δὲ Καῒν καὶ ταῖς θυσίαις αὐτοῦ οὐ προσέσχεν·» ἐφορᾷ γὰρ ὅτι τὸ ἁνδάνον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀποστρέφεται μισῶν τὸ μὴ οὕτως ἔχον, οὐκ ἀσυμφανές. Ἐπιτιθεμένων δὲ τῷ μόσχῳ τῶν χειρῶν τοῦ διημαρτηκότος, ἡ σφαγὴ πράττεται· καὶ ἐνώπιον Κυρίου. «Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἡμῶν αἴρει τὰς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται» σφαζόμενος. Ἔργου γὰρ δὴ καὶ πράξεων, ἡ χεὶρ, εἰς τύπον. Πλὴν, ἐνώπιον Κυρίου σφάζεται, μονονουχὶ καὶ συγκαταβαίνοντος τοῦ Πατρὸς εἰς τὸ δεῖν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐκτεθνάναι τὸν Υἱόν· οὐ γὰρ ἀποστρέφεται σφαζόμενον βλέπων, καὶ οὐ δή που πάντως τὸ παθεῖν ἐπαινῶν, οὐκ ἠγνοηκὼς δὲ ὅτι σωτήριόν ἐστι τῷ κόσμῳ τὸ παθεῖν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ. Οὐκοῦν αὐτὸς ἡμῶν αἴρει τὰς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, τὴν ἐπὶ τῷ τιμίῳ σταυρῷ δι' ἡμᾶς ὑπομένων σφαγήν. Εἶτα λαβὼν ὁ ἱερεὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τῷ δακτύλῳ, ῥανεῖ μὲν ἑπτάκις ἐπὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τὸ ἅγιον, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κιβωτοῦ. Ὄνομα δὲ αὐτῷ, τὸ ἱλαστήριον. Καταχρίει δὲ καὶ τὰ κέρατα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος. Γέγονε γὰρ ἡμῖν ἱλασμός τε καὶ ἱλαστήριον, ὁ Χριστός. Πλὴν, ἐν αἵματι διαθήκης αἰωνίου, τελεωτάτην ἡμῖν δωρεῖται τὴν ἀποκάθαρσιν. Τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ, τὸ ἑπτάκις ῥαίνεσθαι τῷ αἵματι τὸ ἱλαστήριον· σύμβολον δὲ τελειότητος, ὁ ἑπτὰ ἀριθμός. Εὐωδιάζει γὰρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ θάνατος τὴν τοῦ κόσμου σωτηρίαν καὶ ζωὴν καὶ τὴν ἐν πίστει προσαγωγήν· «Εἷς γὰρ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν, ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν, ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι,» κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Οὐκοῦν τοῦ θανάτου τὴν εὐωδίαν δηλοῖ τὸ καταχρίεσθαι τῷ αἵματι τὸ χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον. Ἐκχεῖται δὲ καὶ τὸ αἷμα τὸ λοιπὸν παρὰ τὴν βάσιν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τῶν καρπω
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing 19: that Christ is cleansing (κάθαρσις) of priests and people, for we have been justified in him] rubbing off (ἀποτρίβω) the defilement (μολυσμός) from sin, would be clear (σαφές) to anyone also through these. Let us say part by part (ἀνὰ μέρος) the things on each of the written things; for the account would proceed distinctly (εὐκρινῶς) and unfolding (διαπτύσσω), as is possible, the hidden things. PALL. You said well. CYR. The calf (μόσχος) is taken unblemished (ἀμώμητος) and unstruck (ἀπλήξ) into a type (τύπος) of Christ the truly unblemished (ἄμωμος), who did not endure (ἀνέχομαι) to suffer the wounding (τραυματισμός) from sin. 'For the ruler of this world comes, and will find nothing in me'; for he did not do sin, according to the Scriptures. It is brought to the very doors of the holy tent before the Lord, [he] as it were not refusing (παραιτέομαι) to suffer for the holy tent, i.e. the Church, and dedicated (ἀνατίθημι) for her into an odour of fragrance (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας) to God and Father. Therefore he said: 'For them I sanctify (ἁγιάζω) myself', saying 'sanctify' instead of 'bring forward (προσάγω)' and 'dedicate an unblemished offering (προσφορά)'. For what is dedicated to God is said to be sanctified, as written: 'A snare (παγίς) to a man quickly to sanctify something of his own; for after vowing (εὔχομαι) it comes to repenting (μετανοέω)'. That the offering is acceptable (δεκτή) and well-pleasing (εὐάρεστος) the 'before the Lord' shows. We understand the thing written on the pair (ξυνωρίς) of brothers, Cain and Abel: 'God looked upon (ἐπεῖδον) Abel and his gifts, but to Cain and his sacrifices he did not attend (προσέχω)'. That he looks upon (ἐφοράω) what pleases (ἁνδάνω) him and turns away (ἀποστρέφομαι) hating what is not so, is not unclear (ἀσυμφανές). The hands of the one who sinned (διαμαρτάνω) being laid on the calf, the slaughter (σφαγή) is done, and before the Lord. 'For he lifts (αἴρω) our sins and is pained (ὀδυνάομαι) for us', being slaughtered. For the hand [is] into a type of work and deeds (πράξεις). But he is slaughtered before the Lord, the Father all but (μονονουχί) consenting (συγκαταβαίνω) to its being necessary that the Son die for us; for he does not turn away seeing him slaughtered, not indeed at all praising (ἐπαινέω) the suffering, but not ignorant that it is saving (σωτήριον) to the world that Emmanuel suffer for us. So he lifts our sins and is pained for us, enduring the slaughter on the precious (τίμιος) cross for us. Then the priest taking of the blood with the finger will sprinkle (ῥαίνω) seven times on the holy veil (καταπέτασμα) which was over the ark (κιβωτός); its name the mercy seat (ἱλαστήριον). He smears (καταχρίω) also the horns (κέρατα) of the altar of incense (θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θυμιάματος). For Christ has become for us propitiation (ἱλασμός) and mercy seat. But in blood of an eternal covenant (διαθήκη αἰώνιος) he gifts us most perfect (τελεώτατος) cleansing (ἀποκάθαρσις). This, I think, is the mercy seat being sprinkled seven times; seven is a symbol (σύμβολον) of perfection (τελειότης). For his death also is fragrant (εὐωδιάζω) [with] the salvation and life of the world and the access (προσαγωγή) in faith: 'One died for all, that the living no longer live to themselves but to the one who died for them and was raised', according to the Scriptures. So the smearing of the golden censer/altar (θυμιατήριον) with blood shows the fragrance of the death. The remaining blood is poured out by the base (βάσις) of the altar of burnt offerings (καρπώματα)...
pass_b_english: Cyril: …will be clear to anyone from these things too. But let us take up, one by one, what belongs to each point of the text; for so the discussion would go forward clearly and unfold, as far as it can, what is hidden.

Cyril: The calf, then, is taken without blemish and without wound (Leviticus 4:3) as a type of Christ, who is truly without blemish and did not submit to the wound that sin inflicts. ‘For the ruler of this world is coming,’ he says, ‘and he will find nothing in me’ (John 14:30); for he committed no sin, as the Scriptures say (1 Peter 2:22). And it is brought to the very doors of the holy tent, before the Lord (Leviticus 4:4); so Christ, as it were, did not refuse to suffer for the holy tent, that is, the Church, and was dedicated for her as a fragrant aroma to God the Father (Ephesians 5:2). That is why he said, ‘For their sake I sanctify myself’ (John 17:19). By ‘I sanctify’ he means ‘I bring and dedicate an unblemished offering to God the Father.’ For whatever is dedicated to God is said to be sanctified, as in the saying somewhere in Scripture: ‘It is a snare to a man to sanctify hastily something of his own, for after he has made the vow he comes to regret it’ (Proverbs 20:25). The words ‘before the Lord’ show that the offering is acceptable and well pleasing. For we already know what is written about the pair of brothers, I mean Cain and Abel: ‘God looked upon Abel and upon his gifts,’ it says, ‘but to Cain and his sacrifices he paid no heed’ (Genesis 4:4–5). For it is plain enough that God looks upon what pleases him, and turns away in hatred from what does not. When the hands of the one who has sinned have been laid on the calf, the slaughter is carried out, and that before the Lord (Leviticus 4:4). For ‘he takes away our sins and suffers pain for us’ (Isaiah 53:4) as he is slain; for the hand stands as a type of deeds and actions. Yet he is slain before the Lord, the Father all but consenting that the Son must die for us. For the Father does not turn away when he sees him slain; not that he in any way praises the suffering, but he knows well that Emmanuel’s suffering for us brings salvation to the world. So it is he who takes away our sins and suffers pain for us (Isaiah 53:4), enduring for our sake the slaughter on the precious cross. Then the priest takes some of the blood on his finger and sprinkles it seven times on the holy veil (Leviticus 4:6), which was over the ark, and whose name is the mercy seat. He also smears the horns of the altar of incense (Leviticus 4:7). For Christ has become for us both atonement (1 John 2:2) and mercy seat (Romans 3:25). Yet it is in the blood of an eternal covenant (Hebrews 13:20) that he grants us the most perfect cleansing. This, I think, is the meaning of the mercy seat being sprinkled seven times with the blood, for the number seven is a sign of perfection. For his death too is fragrant with the salvation and life of the world, and with our access to God in faith. ‘For one died for all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and was raised’ (2 Corinthians 5:14–15), as the Scriptures say. So the smearing of the golden altar of incense with the blood shows the fragrance of his death. The rest of the blood is poured out at the base of the altar of burnt offerings (Leviticus 4:7)…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, continuing Cyril's turn from section 19 ('But that Christ is the cleansing of priests and people alike, for we have been justified in him, ...'); the 'Cyril: …' label follows the Book 10 continuation convention. ἀπλήξ ('unstruck', 'without wound') is Cyril's own word beside ἄμωμος; Leviticus 4:3 has only ἄμωμος, so the citation marks the unblemished calf. John 14:30: Cyril reads εὑρήσει οὐδέν ('will find nothing') where the Gospel text has οὐκ ἔχει οὐδέν; translated as Cyril has it. 'He committed no sin' cited to 1 Peter 2:22 (exact wording; it echoes Isaiah 53:9). Ephesians 5:2 cited for ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας applied to Christ's self-offering. Proverbs 20:25 is the LXX text (same verse number in English Bibles, though the Hebrew sense differs). The clause 'ἐφορᾷ γὰρ ὅτι τὸ ἁνδάνον ... οὐκ ἀσυμφανές' has awkward word order in PG; read as 'that he looks upon what pleases him ... is not unclear', so the γάρ is left implicit. Isaiah 53:4 is LXX (οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται); Cyril writes αἴρει ('takes away'), perhaps under John 1:29; rendered as he has it. The subject of the slaughter sentences shifts from the calf to Christ (masculine participles), so 'he' is used. Cyril identifies the 'holy veil' of Leviticus 4:6 (where the LXX has κατὰ τὸ καταπέτασμα, 'before the veil') with something over the ark called the mercy seat; translated as he states it, not harmonised. θυμιατήριον here means the golden altar of incense (as in Hebrews 9:4), not a hand censer. 'Access in faith' (προσαγωγή) may echo Romans 5:2 or Ephesians 3:12; left uncited as doubtful. The section ends mid-word (καρπω|μάτων); English closes the phrase 'altar of burnt offerings' here, and section 21 resumes with 'in the outer tent'.
